content:
maya: P95 GPU errors jumped in the p4d heterogeneous pool at 03:07 UTC — Xid 31 and a handful of Xid 13s.
maya: Alert: https://metrics.internal/redwood/gpu-errors?from=03:00&to=03:30 — see the burst around 03:07
ops-bot: Deploy alert triggered: gpu-error-rate > 5/min for cluster=p4d-hetero in us-west-2 :rotating_light:
ajay: We landed the mixed-driver rollout (540 kernel modules + 535 compat shim) last night. Could be mismatch.
lin: grabbing dmesg from affected host-12 now, tail -n 200 | grep -i Xid
lin: ```
[  912.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 31, pid=0, GPU 0: Xid meaning: thermal/driver timeout
[  912.123789] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus
[  912.124000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 13, pid=3456, GPU 0: Xid meaning: memory access fault
```
tess: Host list sample (10 nodes) shows errors concentrated on a subset that landed new kernel-5.19.0-rcX yesterday.
kyle: So it's in the intersection: driver 540 + kernel 5.19 variant. Heterogeneous fleet + version skew = repro risk.
maya: Current impact: small spike but high error severity -> some job restarts, higher retry traffic. Unit tests for large-batch inference started seeing tail latency > SLO.
ajay: Suggested next steps from ops playbook: 1) isolate machines with kernel 5.19 + driver 540, 2) divert new inference traffic via traffic-router, 3) collect full dmesg + nvidia-smi -q, 4) open infra-incident if >10% hosts affected.
lin: Collected nvidia-smi snapshot on host-12:
lin: ```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR
GPU 0
    Xid Errors
        Xid 31: 7
        Xid 13: 2
    Persistence-M: Enabled
    Driver Version: 540.51.06
```
ops-bot: Note: There is an ongoing NCCL watchdog alert in us-west-2 but current metric correlation is weak (only a few hosts show watchdog timeouts).
sre-bot: Recommend running the compatibility probe on a canary subset: 3 hosts with 540 + kernel 5.19 under synthetic collective workload (nccl-tests/all_reduce) for 30m.
tess: I'll spin up canary jobs. Provisioning note: p4d capacity in us-west-2 limited; we should reuse stopped canaries in staging to avoid cost/spill.
ajay: If canary repros, rollback plan: revert driver to 535 on affected pool via rolling reboot (2 nodes at a time) and hold for 24h.
kyle: Also consider temporary routing policy: route large-batch traffic to us-east-1 where the fleet is homogeneous and driver 535 is stable.
maya: Action items: Tess -> run canary and attach logs (due in 30m). Lin -> build host list and collect full logs (due in 15m). Ajay -> draft rollback runbook and standby for decision. Ops-bot -> throttle new large-batch jobs to soft-limit.
ops-bot: Throttling applied: large-batch queue limited to 50% for us-west-2
tess: Canary started on staging-hosts: nccl-tests all_reduce 1k iter, attaching logs to thread when done
maya: Thanks — if canary reproduces we trigger infra-incident and follow rollback. If not, we'll keep monitoring and relax throttles in 2 hours.
ajay: Also adding note to docs: heterogeneous fleets + kernel skews are a known risk. We'll add a preflight probe in the driver rollout checklist.
kyle: cc @security — if we start mass reboots we should coordinate maintenance window for customers on Dedicated clusters.
maya: closing loop: will ping again with canary result. :eyes:"
